text:
sarah: Heads-up — after the tokenizer v2.2 rollout at 09:10 UTC we’re seeing a p95 latency jump on the gpt-like pool, ~40% higher. Throughput down ~25%. KV cache hit rate dropped from 82% -> 51% on pod group A. Anyone else seeing this?
devon: saw the alert. correlates with canary traffic. timeline matches the tokenizer change.
maria: quick datapoints: mean tokens/request increased 1.7x on affected traffic, median not as bad but tail shifted. seq-len distribution moved right because punctuation splitting changed.
tony: interesting — that could increase KV cache churn. if prefix keys differ we evict more often. can we repro with a controlled load?
sarah: repro harness running now with tokenization v2.1 vs v2.2 against same prompts. devon, can you attach profiler?
devon: attaching short flame graph/snippet from sampling profiler (core GPU kernels):
```
hotspots: matmul_opt (36%) | matmul_generic (22%) | kv_lookup (18%) | copy_gdr (9%) | other (15%)
note: matmul_generic usage shot up post-rollout — kernel selector falling back for many workloads
```

devon: kernel selector logs show many small batches now pick the generic matmul_kernel due to a new shape-profile path. selector heuristic threshold triggered because avg seq len changed and pad distribution changed.
lee: also saw increased PCIe copies at start-of-inference for longer sequences — per-request memcpy cost increased.
maria: KV cache logs: eviction rate per-request doubled. cache_key mismatch rate up ~30% because tokenization produces slightly different subword splits for URLs and email-like tokens.
tony: could be two things: tokenizer producing different token boundary for common prefixes -> cache key variance; and longer sequences causing more keys stored per request -> early eviction.
infra-bot: rolling metric: deploy canary at 09:10 (tokenizer:v2.2) -> 09:22 p95 spike -> 09:28 mitigation started.
devon: quick experiment: forced model routing to pinned kernel (matmul_opt) with selector override on one canary instance. p95 dropped back ~18% but not fully to baseline. suggests both kernel fallback + KV thrash.
sarah: deploy-bot can we rollback canary?
deploy-bot: canary rollback initiated by @sarah at 09:38 UTC :white_check_mark:

maria: after rollback p95 back to ~+5% vs baseline. KV hit rate recovered to 79%.
lee: I captured a trace showing repeated KV miss for same prefix within ~120s window — indicates we were not reusing cached prefixes because tokenization changed representation.
ton y: (typo in name corrected: tony) We should add a deterministic normalizer for canonical token boundaries in the serving stack so tokenizer variants don't change cache keys.
maria: agree. short-term mitigations: 1) rollback (done), 2) pin kernel selector to prefer matmul_opt for this model family while we tune heuristics, 3) add tokenizer-aware cache key normalization in runtime.
devon: opened perf issue: INF-8743 — includes profiler artifacts, kernel-selector logs, kv eviction traces, and repro harness.
sarah: next steps: eng-ml to check tokenizer diff and produce mapping table; eng-runtime to add cache key normalizer PR; infra to add temporary kernel selector override flag per-pool.
lee: one more datapoint — noisy neighbor effect: a tenant on same node increased concurrent tiny requests (short seqs but very high qps) which made selector see mixed profile and choose conservative kernels more often. when we split tenant traffic to different pools, the fallback rate dropped. split test documented in infra ticket INF-8746.
ton y: also let's run synthetic loads with skewed seq-length distributions in QA to catch these regressions earlier. add a check in rollout playbook: monitor mean tokens/request and KV hit rate in the first 30 minutes and auto-hold rollout if hit-rate drops >15% or p95 increases >20%.
maria: PR for key normalizer draft: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/562. includes canonicalization rules for URLs, emails, and punctuation-run collapsing.
devon: added temporary metric dashboard: rollout_token_change -> mean_tokens, kv_hit_rate, kernel_fallback_rate, p95_latency. link: https://dash.local/d/rollouts/tokenizer-v2.2-investigation
sarah: thanks team. Let's keep this thread for short updates. If anyone reproduces different vectors (quantization mismatch, CPU fallback), post here. :thumbsup:
